Proxy-Cheap wins on price by a wide margin: about $7.80 for 10 GB at its current promotional rate against $52.50 at IPRoyal, with no subscription. For moderate-difficulty scraping and country-level work, that is hard to beat. IPRoyal is worth the premium when you need city or state targeting, very long sticky sessions for account management, or a provider with a longer track record in independent benchmarks. A sensible approach is to test Proxy-Cheap on your targets first and only move to IPRoyal if success rates or targeting fall short.

IPRoyal and Proxy-Cheap both sell to price-conscious buyers, but they compete in different ways. Proxy-Cheap is currently advertising rotating residential traffic at $0.78/GB with no monthly plan, one of the lowest prices on the market. IPRoyal costs several times more per gigabyte at small volumes but offers city targeting, sticky sessions up to seven days and traffic that never expires. Both also sell cheap static ISP and datacenter IPs. Here is how to choose between the cheapest option and the more feature-rich one.

blocks.text: IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: IPRoyal vs Proxy-Cheap

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

At 10 GB a month, Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper option at about $7.80 against $52.50 for IPRoyal, roughly 85% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; Proxy-Cheap comes to about $78. The sticker price is only half of it. IPRoyal's unused traffic carries forward, while Proxy-Cheap's does not (pay-as-you-go balance, no monthly commitment), so if your usage swings from month to month IPRoyal can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. IPRoyal lists '32M+' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, IPRoyal lists 195 countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification), while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. How Proxy-Cheap compares: fine for country-level price checks.

Ad verification and geo-testing: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts. How Proxy-Cheap compares: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.

Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test IPRoyal and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle IPRoyal vs Proxy-Cheap faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).

2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day. 3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, IPRoyal comes out ahead in 4, Proxy-Cheap in 1, and 1 is a tie. That makes IPRoyal the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
